_note: Zerodha design guide (Brand guidelines.pdf, 2025). Every value traces to the guide; deviations are listed in _deviations. Palettes validated with the dataviz validator on #FFFFFF.
_deviations: Acronyms of six or more letters listed in brand.acronyms (EBITDA) are allowed: they are the standard names of measures, not all-caps styling, which stays banned (owner decision, 5 Nov 2026).
Sunshine yellow #FFA412 -> #F59A0C as a data colour: #FFA412 fails the lightness band for marks (guide permits adjustments for accessibility). #FFA412 stays the brand colour elsewhere.
Map ramp's darkest warm step #C24E1C is a shade of #F07339, needed so the top bin reads as distinct (accessibility clause). All other ramp steps are brand colours or tints.
Label and micro-text colours #9B9B9B/#CCCCCC/#888888 fail WCAG 4.5:1 at 20px on white, so small text uses #666666 (approved body colour). Light greys are used only for lines and fills.
Axis labels, notes and source are body minus 4px: the guide's ±4px adjustment for smaller text. Core sizes (headline, body) stay on the guide's 8-point scale, e.g. 40 and 24 on 1080px feed canvases.

Tracking: Inter at our sizes is set with slight negative letter-spacing (-0.015em headline, -0.006em elsewhere), eased from Inter's dynamic-metrics values after the owner found the tighter setting looked clamped. The guide is silent on tracking; this is typesetting, not stylisation.

Map/tile ramp's strongest cool step is #2A64A9 (the guide's own blue shadow colour) instead of #387ED1: white labels on #387ED1 reach only 4.1:1, short of 4.5:1 for small text (accessibility clause). #387ED1 remains the series blue.

Side (landscape) layouts give the header column 30% of the width; for fixed-shape charts (maps, tile grids) that cannot use the extra width, the frame widens the header column up to 45% rather than leave an empty band.

Filled cells and bars that carry white text (rank grids, tiles) use #2A64A9, the guide's blue shadow colour, as the series blue: white on #387ED1 is 4.1:1, short of 4.5:1 for small text. Lines and unlabelled marks keep #387ED1. Token: color.accent_fill.
name: zerodha

margin._note: Equal outer margin on every side, 4.5% of the canvas's short side (was 6%; the owner found 6% wasted canvas on 3 Nov 2026); platform safe zones add to it.

color._note: Colour tokens. Chart marks use only grammar.ink greys or series colours (lint 'grammar'); other, nodata_stroke and axis are aliases kept for older chart code and equal grammar inks.

type._note: Type roles (the grammar). step picks the format's headline/body/small size; colour is fixed per role. White (#FFFFFF) may replace a role's colour only on a dark fill. Chart text (inside g.chart) is set with tabular figures; header and footer prose keeps proportional figures. Lint 'grammar' checks every text matches a role.

label_on_fill._why: Labels inside a filled mark (tiles): semibold so white text on a series colour passes contrast as large text.

space._note: Use-of-space targets checked by lint 'space'. Shares are of the whole canvas; safe zones are excluded. Formats may override in formats.json 'space'. band_max_lines 1.25: the header-to-chart and chart-to-footer breaks must read as breaks; one dek line is the floor, a quarter more is the ceiling.

style._note: House style checks (lint 'style'). extra_strokes: weights at k=1 allowed besides theme.marks (white rings round dots, white outlines between map regions).

gaps._note: Header/footer gaps are grammar.gaps step names.
gaps.headline: l

header._note: max_lines: the frame picks the first copy variant that fits; none fitting is a COPY error, never smaller type. Side layouts: headline at most 3 lines; notes go in the header column when they fit the space left between dek and source (the column has no dead gap).
header._note_stack_on_wide: Landscape (side) formats use a stacked header when it takes at most this share of the height inside the margins; fixed-shape charts keep the side column.
header._headline_why: Headlines are never narrowed (no balance, no widow narrowing): the owner read narrowed first lines as clamped on 28 Oct, 3 Nov and 4 Nov. Lint 'headline' flags a line that the next word would have fitted on, and one-word last lines; widows are fixed with copy variants.

marks._note: Stroke widths and dot radius in px at k=1. Every data stroke uses one of these (lint 'style').

grammar._note: The visual grammar. Every chart reads its ink, spacing and mark geometry from here (kit.js K.ink, K.sp, K.mk); CLAUDE.md 'Visual grammar' has the rules in words. Pixel values are at k=1 (body 24px).

ink._note: How dark each kind of mark is, loudest first. Only hero marks carry hue; one thing per chart is loud.

space._note: Spacing steps at k=1. Every gap in frame, kit and templates is one of these (lint_code checks the source). Names say the size, not the use.

gaps._note: Which step each recurring gap in the chart uses. Header and footer gaps (topper, headline, dek-to-chart, chart-to-footer) are step names in header.gaps.

mark._note: Mark geometry at k=1. bar_ratio: bar thickness as a share of its row or column slot (the rest is gap), at most bar_max. row_max: the tallest row a horizontal bar chart may have; past it the form turns to columns (bridge) rather than float bars in air. min_mark: the thinnest bar or step drawn, so a tiny value still shows. leader_min: shortest leader worth drawing. swarm_fill_lo/hi_ratio: the share of the room across the value axis a beeswarm aims to fill; swarm_gap_max_ratio: how far dot spacing may loosen (× diameter) to get there. column_ratio: column width as a share of its slot in a time series of columns (many slots, so the columns sit close).

axis._note: Ticks at least label_gap label-heights apart, between ticks_min and ticks_max of them, and they must cover the data: neither end of the data lies more than half a step beyond the outermost tick (stretch_max).
axis._note_y_cover: Value axes drawn as horizontal gridlines stretch up to a full step (y_cover 1), so the data never runs past the top or bottom gridline: the owner found a line poking above its top gridline odd (3 Nov 2026). Horizontal value axes (swarms, ranked dots, range bars) keep stretch_max, where a full step of padding is dead canvas. Data within touch (0.1) of a step past a gridline is left there: it reads as touching the line, and a whole extra step for it is dead canvas.

devices._note: Visual devices a note may name, and the SVG evidence that the chart draws them. A note that names a device the chart does not draw is a COPY error at render and a lint 'grammar' issue.

headline._note: Plain headlines (render COPY check on every variant). One statement a reader gets in one pass: the finding, in the words a person would say it. Numbers and context go to the dek (the sub-heading). No front-loaded figures ('At +2.16°C, ...'), no 'Even ...', no two-part constructions joined by a colon or semicolon, no questions or exclamations.

no_break._note: Names that never break across lines, in any frame text (headline, dek, box, notes, source). The frame swaps their spaces for no-break spaces before wrapping.
